The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
node_mark_all(child, mark);
```
```c
node_set_marks(node, offset, child, marks);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because when a new node is created to replace an entry with search marks set, the function `node_mark_all(child, mark)` incorrectly sets the search mark on all entries in the newly created node. This is appropriate only for splits to order 0, but when splitting to a larger order, sibling entries should not inherit these marks, leading to incorrect mark propagation.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
node_mark_slots(child, sibs, mark);
```
```c
node_set_marks(node, offset, child, xas->xa_sibs, marks);
```
Reason:
The fix involves replacing the incorrect call to `node_mark_all(child, mark)` with `node_mark_slots(child, sibs, mark)`, which correctly sets the search marks only on the appropriate entries based on the number of siblings. Additionally, the function `node_set_marks` is updated to pass the correct number of siblings, ensuring that only the intended entries receive the search marks, thus preventing incorrect mark propagation when splitting to a larger order.
